subject: Medical Triads
title: Renal & Endocrine Triads
preview: Four classic renal/endocrine patterns—HUS, Whipple triad, pheochromocytoma and mixed cryoglobulinemia—are most useful when connected to mechanisms.

sections.title: HUS: hematology meets the kidney
points: Small-vessel injury produces red-cell fragmentation, thrombocytopenia and kidney dysfunction.
A diarrheal prodrome can occur in Shiga-toxin-associated HUS but is not present in every thrombotic microangiopathy.

sections.title: Whipple triad: confirm true hypoglycemia
points: Document compatible symptoms, low circulating glucose during symptoms, and improvement after glucose correction.
The triad characterizes genuine symptomatic hypoglycemia; it does not establish insulinoma as the cause by itself.

sections.title: Pheochromocytoma and cryoglobulinemia
points: Episodic headache + sweating + palpitations is the classic pheochromocytoma memory pattern.
Meltzer triad in mixed cryoglobulinemia is palpable purpura, arthralgia and weakness; other causes can produce similar features.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Do not diagnose a specific endocrine tumor solely from a triad.
An apparently characteristic presentation still requires appropriate biochemical or hematologic confirmation.

quickRevision: Hemolytic uremic syndrome classically combines microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury.
Whipple triad requires compatible symptoms, measured low glucose at the time of symptoms and relief when glucose is corrected.
Pheochromocytoma can cause episodic headache, sweating, palpitations and hypertension.

quiz.question: The triad of headache, sweating and palpitations suggests which endocrine syndrome?
quiz.explanation: Catecholamine release in pheochromocytoma classically causes episodic headache, sweating and palpitations; blood pressure may rise substantially during episodes.
